The rain doesn't fall here the way it does in other places. It arrives like a secret, first as a hush over the rooftops, then as silver threads that catch the streetlights and turn them into trembling constellations. I've been watching it from this window for three hours now, notebook open, pen idle, because some moments refuse to be written while they're happening.

There's a cat on the fire escape across the alley who seems to share my opinion. She's been sitting in the exact same spot, completely unbothered by the weather, looking like she's conducting an orchestra only she can hear. I respect that kind of commitment to one's own rhythm.

Sometimes I think about how every person walking below me is carrying an entire universe in their chest. All those private heartbreaks and ridiculous hopes, the songs they can't get out of their heads, the way they pronounce certain words wrong on purpose because it reminds them of their grandmother. We're all just temporary constellations of memory and want, passing through each other's orbits for fractions of seconds.

The rain has slowed to a whisper now. The cat has vanished, probably to attend to whatever mysterious business cats conduct at 2:17 a.m. I should probably sleep. Instead I'll make tea and read that poem I love until the words start swimming. Some nights aren't meant for productivity. They're meant for remembering that we're allowed to simply exist inside the beautiful strangeness of being alive.

(Word count: 248)
